The course is aimed at students at LTH who want to activate and develop the French they have acquired from high-school or from LU's beginner courses in French. The course mainly provides oral and written skills training, both in comprehension, production and interaction, but also covers basic knowledge of French society and French culture based on the texts included. The main features of French grammar are reviewed and practiced through reading various texts in French and through one's own written production. Specialized texts are studied in terms of both content and language. Current topics linked to French social life are discussed in class and in small groups. Training is also given in discussing one's own specialist area. Since practice in oral language skills is an important part of the course, active participation in the teaching is required.
Module 1
This module includes a widened knowledge of spoken French. French society and culture, 3,5 credits
Module 2
Widened knowledge of written French and grammar, 4 credits.

Grading scale: TH - (U, 3, 4, 5) - (Fail, Three, Four, Five)
Assessment:
One compulsory oral presentation (module 1), a written examination in written language skills (module 2).

The examiner, in consultation with Disability Support Services, may deviate from the regular form of examination in order to provide a permanently disabled student with a form of examination equivalent to that of a student without a disability.

Modules
Code: 0119. Name: Oral Proficiency, French Society and Culture . 

Credits: 3.5. Grading scale: TH - (U, 3, 4, 5).
        
          Assessment: An oral presentation
        
        
        
        
Code: 0219. Name: Written Proficiency and Literary Texts. 

Credits: 4.0. Grading scale: TH - (U, 3, 4, 5).
        
          Assessment: One written examen.
